content.user_title: Analyze Mass Spectrometry Data with pyOpenMS
content.value_statement: Mass spectrometry workflows require many OpenMS objects, file formats, and algorithms. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical pyOpenMS guidance for proteomics and metabolomics analysis.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to load mzML, mzXML, idXML, mzTab, FASTA, featureXML, and consensusXML files.
Guides signal processing with smoothing, filtering, normalization, and peak picking examples.
Explains feature detection, alignment, linking, and consensus map workflows.
Covers peptide and protein identification, FDR filtering, and protein inference workflows.
Provides metabolomics examples for annotation, normalization, quality control, imputation, and table export.
Explains core pyOpenMS data structures and parameter handling.
limitations: It does not run analyses unless the user asks the agent to execute code.
It assumes pyOpenMS and needed search engines are installed in the working environment.
It provides examples, not validation of biological conclusions or instrument settings.
Large LC-MS/MS datasets may require local compute resources outside the skill.

use_cases.title: Process Identification Results
use_cases.description: Apply pyOpenMS guidance to load idXML data, inspect peptide hits, filter by FDR, and save reviewed results.

use_cases.title: Prepare Metabolomics Tables
use_cases.description: Build workflows for feature annotation, blank filtering, missing value handling, normalization, and export for statistics.

use_cases.title: Prototype Analysis Pipelines
use_cases.description: Use documented pyOpenMS objects and file formats to draft reproducible LC-MS/MS processing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Load an mzML File
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to load an mzML file with pyOpenMS and summarize the spectra, chromatograms, retention times, and peak counts.

prompt_templates.title: Filter Peptide Identifications
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me load idXML identification results, apply a one percent FDR filter, inspect peptide hits, and save filtered results.

prompt_templates.title: Build Feature Detection Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a pyOpenMS workflow for centroided LC-MS data that performs smoothing, feature detection, retention time alignment, and feature linking.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Metabolomics Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a full untargeted metabolomics workflow with pyOpenMS, including feature detection, annotation, normalization, QC filtering, imputation, and table export.

output_examples.input: I need to inspect a new mzML file before analysis.
output_examples.output: The skill can outline a pyOpenMS inspection workflow that loads the file, counts spectra, checks MS levels, reviews retention times, and reports peak counts.

output_examples.input: I have peptide identification results and need a one percent FDR filter.
output_examples.output: The skill can describe the FDR workflow: load idXML results, apply FalseDiscoveryRate, keep hits with q-values at or below 0.01, and store filtered results.

output_examples.input: I want an analysis-ready metabolomics table from a consensus map.
output_examples.output: The skill can guide table creation with m/z, retention time, feature identifiers, sample intensities, normalization steps, and quality control checks.

best_practices: Confirm file formats and centroiding status before choosing processing algorithms.
Record parameter values for smoothing, peak picking, alignment, and feature detection.
Use target-decoy or q-value workflows when reporting peptide and protein identifications.
anti_patterns: Do not treat example file names as real project paths without checking your workspace.
Do not compare search engine scores without confirming each engine score direction.
Do not draw biological conclusions from feature tables without domain review and quality controls.

faq.question: What is pyOpenMS?
faq.answer: pyOpenMS is the Python interface to OpenMS for computational mass spectrometry workflows.

faq.question: Which data formats does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers common OpenMS formats such as mzML, mzXML, idXML, mzTab, FASTA, featureXML, and consensusXML.

faq.question: Can it run search engines for peptide identification?
faq.answer: It explains integration patterns, but external search engines must be installed and configured separately.

faq.question: Does it support metabolomics workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for feature annotation, normalization, blank filtering, imputation, and table export.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it validate scientific results?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and examples, while scientific validation remains the user responsibility.
